tasks.title: Lecture #15
tasks.instruction: Listen to a short talk on architecture.
tasks.transcript:
Before starting our tour of Monticello, I'd like to give you some historical facts that might help you appreciate what you see today even more.
Monticello was the very much loved home of Thomas Jefferson for over fifty years. Jefferson, who was, of course, President, was also a great reader and language enthusiast. He read widely on different subjects, including architecture.
He wasn't formally trained in architecture, but as a result of his study and observation of other buildings, he was able to help design and build the house.
He chose the site himself, naming the estate "Monticello," which means "little mountain" in Italian. In fact, many of the ideas behind the design also came from the Italian architect Andrea Palladio, who lived in the sixteenth century and who had a great influence on the architecture of England.
Jefferson, however, ignored one of Palladio's principles --- that is, not to build in a high place. Monticello's elevation made the transportation of what was needed at the house --- for example, food --- especially difficult. But the view from the estate would not be as spectacular if Jefferson had followed Palladio's advice;
there really is no boundary between the house and the nature around it, and so Jefferson was able to look out on his beloved state of Virginia from his wonderful vantage point. Now we'll go on to Jefferson's library.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the talk?

options.A: To explain the historical significance of Monticello
options.B: To discuss Thomas Jefferson's contributions to architecture
options.C: To describe Jefferson's love of reading and how it influenced his architecture
options.D: To give background information about Monticello before a tour

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：这段讲话的主要目的是什么？ 定位原文： Before starting our tour of Monticello, I'd like to give you some historical facts that might help you appreciate what you see today even more. 选项分析： A. To explain the historical significance of Monticello（解释蒙蒂塞洛的历史意义）。讲话提供了背景信息，但未重点阐述其历史意义，所以A选项错误。 B. To discuss Thomas Jefferson's contributions to architecture（讨论托马斯·杰斐逊对建筑的贡献）。讲话提到杰斐逊参与设计，但主要目的是介绍蒙蒂塞洛的背景，而非全面讨论其建筑贡献，所以B选项错误。 C. To describe Jefferson's love of reading and how it influenced his architecture（描述杰斐逊对阅读的热爱及其如何影响他的建筑）。讲话提到杰斐逊广泛阅读，但这是背景信息的一部分，并非主要目的，所以C选项错误。 D. To give background information about Monticello before a tour（在游览前提供关于蒙蒂塞洛的背景信息）。讲话开篇明确说明在开始游览前提供历史事实，因此D选项正确。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what influence did Andrea Palladio have on Jefferson's design for Monticello?

options.A: Palladio taught Jefferson how to formally train as an architect
options.B: Palladio's design principles influenced the choice of Monticello's site
options.C: Palladio's ideas about architecture shaped the design of Monticello's structure
options.D: Palladio recommended that Jefferson build Monticello in a low area

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：根据演讲者，安德烈亚·帕拉第奥对杰斐逊设计蒙蒂塞洛有什么影响？ 定位原文： In fact, many of the ideas behind the design also came from the Italian architect Andrea Palladio, who lived in the sixteenth century and who had a great influence on the architecture of England. 选项分析： A. Palladio taught Jefferson how to formally train as an architect（帕拉第奥教杰斐逊如何正式接受建筑师培训）。讲话提到杰斐逊未受过正式建筑训练，且帕拉第奥生活在16世纪，不可能教他，所以A选项错误。 B. Palladio's design principles influenced the choice of Monticello's site（帕拉第奥的设计原则影响了蒙蒂塞洛选址）。讲话提到杰斐逊忽略了帕拉第奥“不在高处建造”的原则，说明选址并非受其影响，所以B选项错误。 C. Palladio's ideas about architecture shaped the design of Monticello's structure（帕拉第奥的建筑理念塑造了蒙蒂塞洛的结构设计）。讲话明确指出设计的许多理念来自帕拉第奥，因此C选项正确。 D. Palladio recommended that Jefferson build Monticello in a low area（帕拉第奥建议杰斐逊在低洼地带建造蒙蒂塞洛）。讲话提到帕拉第奥的原则是不在高处建造，但并未说帕拉第奥本人向杰斐逊提出建议，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: Based on the talk, why did Jefferson ignore Palladio's principle about not building in a high place?

options.A: He believed it would be easier to transport materials
options.B: He wanted a better view of the surrounding nature
options.C: He thought Palladio's advice was outdated
options.D: He preferred to follow his own design principles

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：根据讲话，杰斐逊为什么忽略了帕拉第奥关于不在高处建造的原则？ 定位原文： Monticello's elevation made the transportation of what was needed at the house — for example, food — especially difficult. But the view from the estate would not be as spectacular if Jefferson had followed Palladio's advice; there really is no boundary between the house and the nature around it, and so Jefferson was able to look out on his beloved state of Virginia from his wonderful vantage point. 选项分析： A. He believed it would be easier to transport materials（他认为这样运输材料会更方便）。讲话明确指出高地位置使运输更加困难，所以A选项错误。 B. He wanted a better view of the surrounding nature（他想要更好地欣赏周围的自然景色）。讲话说明如果遵循帕拉第奥的建议，景色就不会如此壮观，暗示杰斐逊为了视野而忽略该原则，因此B选项正确。 C. He thought Palladio's advice was outdated（他认为帕拉第奥的建议过时了）。基于讲话未提及杰斐逊对帕拉第奥建议时效性的看法，所以C选项错误。 D. He preferred to follow his own design principles（他更愿意遵循自己的设计原则）。讲话未说明杰斐逊有自己与之对立的设计原则，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What is the speaker’s attitude towards Jefferson’s decision to build Monticello on a high place?

options.A: The speaker believes Jefferson made a poor decision that caused difficulties.
options.B: The speaker thinks Jefferson's decision was justified because of the spectacular view.
options.C: The speaker criticizes Jefferson for ignoring Palladio's advice.
options.D: The speaker does not give an opinion on Jefferson's decision.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者对杰斐逊在高处建造蒙蒂塞洛的决定持什么态度？ 定位原文： Monticello's elevation made the transportation ... especially difficult. But the view from the estate would not be as spectacular if Jefferson had followed Palladio's advice; there really is no boundary between the house and the nature around it, and so Jefferson was able to look out on his beloved state of Virginia from his wonderful vantage point. 选项分析： A. The speaker believes Jefferson made a poor decision that caused difficulties（演讲者认为杰斐逊做出了一个导致困难的不良决定）。讲话虽承认运输困难，但用“But”转折强调了景色的壮观，并未否定该决定，所以A选项错误。 B. The speaker thinks Jefferson's decision was justified because of the spectacular view（演讲者认为杰斐逊的决定是合理的，因为景色壮观）。讲话明确指出如果没有这个决定景色就不会如此壮观，并用“wonderful vantage point”表达赞赏态度，因此B选项正确。 C. The speaker criticizes Jefferson for ignoring Palladio's advice（演讲者批评杰斐逊忽视了帕拉第奥的建议）。基于讲话并未批评，而是理解并欣赏这一决定，所以C选项错误。 D. The speaker does not give an opinion on Jefferson's decision（演讲者没有对杰斐逊的决定发表看法）。讲话明确表达了对此决定带来的景观效果的欣赏，所以D选项错误
